title: Attach a loose Joy-Con to a docked Nintendo Switch by sliding it down the console's side rail until its catch clicks
instruction: Attach the loose Joy-Con to the console.
context: Households with a Nintendo Switch regularly take its Joy-Con controllers off and put them back, often with the console standing in its TV dock. The Joy-Con's slider enters the console's side rail only at the rail's open top end, and must be pushed all the way down until its sprung catch clicks into a notch. Pressed sideways against the console's side it rests on the rail's lips and does not attach; left above the catch it is on the rail but not locked.
setup: Positions in cm: x ahead of the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midline; heights above the table. Dock (loose, 327 g, black): a Nintendo Switch dock (HAC-007), 173 mm long (along y), 104 mm tall, 54 mm deep, footprint centred at (31.0, -12.0), its lower front wall toward the robot. A slot 16 mm wide runs its full length, open at both ends; its floor is 45 mm above the table; the front wall rises to 75 mm, the back wall to 104 mm, inner top edges rounded 4 mm. A USB-C plug (8.25 x 2.4 x 6.5 mm) stands at the middle of the slot floor. Console (loose, 346 g with its attached Joy-Con): a Nintendo Switch (HAC-001) body, 173 x 102 x 13.9 mm, black, screen glass 137 x 77.2 mm centred on its front face. It stands in the slot, screen toward the robot, its lower edge on the slot floor with its USB-C port (10.0 x 3.6 x 7.0 mm) on the plug, centred over the dock. The blue left Joy-Con (33 mm wide outside the body, 102 x 13.9 mm) is attached to its left (+y) end. Its right (-y) end carries the bare rail: a channel open at the top and closed by a 3 mm stop at the bottom. Two 0.85 mm deep lips leave a 4.7 mm slot; behind them is an 8.7 mm wide cavity, 3.25 mm in from the end face. At the mouth the inner top edges of the lips and cavity walls are rounded 1 mm, and the console's top corner over the channel floor 3 mm. The screen-side lip has a 5 mm notch from 3.5 to 8.5 mm below the console's top. Loose right Joy-Con (red, 52 g): body 102 x 33 x 13.9 mm with a T-slider on its rail face (stem 4.0 mm wide x 1.2 mm, head 8.0 x 1.7 mm, 35.9 mm overall), running from its top end to 3 mm above its bottom end, lower ends rounded; the body's lower inner edge is rounded 3 mm. Its stick (16 mm cap, 8 mm proud) is on its front face, 62 mm below the top. Its catch is a 3 mm round nub, 0.8 mm proud of the rail face beside the stem on the stick side, 6 mm below the top, on a spring (10 g, 2,500 N/m, preloaded 1.25 N, 1 mm travel). The Joy-Con lies on its slider (rail face down), its centre 19.7 mm above the table. Lot A: centred at (19.5, -16.5), long axis along x, top end toward the robot, stick facing the robot's right. Lot B: centred at (17.5, -25.5), long axis along y, top end toward the robot's left, stick facing the robot. Friction (static/dynamic): console and Joy-Con 0.5/0.4, dock 0.7/0.6. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end, except the never rules. 1.0: the Joy-Con on the console's rail within 1 mm of the bottom stop with its catch out in the notch (pushed in no more than 0.25 mm), within 0.6 mm of the rail's line both front to back and in toward the console, parallel to the console within 2 degrees. 0.5: the same line tolerances and at least 30 mm of slider inside the channel, within 3 degrees of parallel, but not seated and clicked (for example stopped on the catch). Both tiers also need: the console still docked (its lower edge within 3 mm of the slot floor, within 8 mm of the slot's centre line and 5 mm of the slot's middle, upright within 3 degrees); no surface of either arm from its third link to the fingertips within 5 mm of the box around the Joy-Con, the console or the dock; the Joy-Con and console still for 1 s (each under 0.2 mm and 0.2 degrees per 0.05 s step). 0: anything else, including a Joy-Con pressed sideways against the console's side, resting on its top, lying on the table, upside down, or still held. Never rules, over the whole trial (any one scores 0): a gripper or fingertip within 1 mm of the screen glass; the console's lower edge more than 5 mm above the slot floor or the console tipped more than 10 degrees; the Joy-Con moving down faster than 0.6 m/s (a fall of about 18 mm); an arm's state unknown. Real trial: seated is the Joy-Con flush with the console's ends after the click; the never rules are judged from the video. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: 1. Seat the console in the dock, screen toward the robot, blue Joy-Con on the robot's left, its port on the dock's plug. 2. Place the dock with its lower wall toward the robot, footprint centred at (31.0, -12.0), length along y. 3. Lay the red Joy-Con on its slider: lot A at (19.5, -16.5) with its top end toward the robot and its stick to the robot's right; lot B at (17.5, -25.5) with its top end to the robot's left and its stick toward the robot. 4. To take it off a real console, hold its release button and slide it up. Run trials on lots A and B in turn.
fidelity: Console, Joy-Con and dock at Nintendo's published sizes and weights, as rigid boxes and cylinders. Rail profile, play (0.35 mm a side), slot and wall heights are estimates. No Joy-Con catch force is published: the catch is a sprung nub needing about 2-3 N extra push (an estimate), and unlike the real one it can be pulled off without the release button. Buttons other than the stick are not modelled. Two lots stop one fixed motion, not a replay of both.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; each hit the 1,200-step limit); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (success at 490 and 582 steps)
